description:
Amazon Leo is Amazon's low Earth orbit satellite network, with a mission to deliver fast, reliable internet connectivity to customers beyond the reach of existing networks. From individual households to schools, hospitals, businesses, and government agencies, Amazon Leo will connect people and organizations operating in locations without reliable connectivity.
The Leo NOC and Leo Incident Management (LIM) Operations Tooling team builds the products that run the Leo network day to day. Our tools are used by the Network Operations Center, Call Leaders, and service teams across Networking, Commerce, and Satellite Operations to see the health of the network, catch problems before customers do, coordinate fast when something goes wrong, and automate the work that slows operators down. We are looking for a Software Development Engineer II to design, build, and operate these tools. You will turn health signals and network telemetry into operator workflows and automation, proactive health and early warning features, NOC dashboards and runbook automation, alarm correlation and noise reduction, incident management and escalation tooling, and the post-event systems that feed every lesson back into better detection. You will work closely with the product manager, operators, and Call Leaders who use your tools every day, and you will own what you build from design through production. 

Key job responsibilities
Design, build, and operate scalable, highly available services and tools that power network operations and incident management for Amazon Leo.
Build proactive health capabilities, including anomaly and trend detection, early warning features, and proactive investigation workflows that help operators act before customers are affected.
Build alarm correlation and deduplication systems so responders see one problem instead of hundreds of alerts.
Build NOC dashboards and operator workflows that bring health, customer impact, affected components, and ongoing events into one view.
Build self-service tooling that lets service teams onboard and manage their own health signals, alarms, and runbooks.
Automate runbook steps, data collection, and repetitive operational tasks so operators spend their time on judgment, not mechanics.
Integrate with observability, telemetry, ticketing, paging, and communication systems across Amazon Leo, including the network observability platform.
Apply automation, machine learning, and generative AI to triage, event summarization, timeline drafting, and correlation where it measurably improves outcomes.
Design systems that stay available when the network they serve is degraded, since operators need these tools most during an outage.
Participate in the full software development lifecycle, including architecture, implementation, testing, deployment, operational readiness, and on-call support.
Mentor other engineers and contribute to a culture of high-quality, secure, and maintainable software.
Export Control Requirement: Due to applicable export control laws and regulations, candidates must be a U.S. citizen or national, U.S. permanent resident (i.e., current Green Card holder), or lawfully admitted into the U.S. as a refugee or granted asylum.

A day in the life
You might start the day with feedback from the NOC on a dashboard you shipped last week and fix a workflow that slowed operators down during an overnight event. Midday, you could be designing a correlation service that groups alarms from many services into a single event, or building the escalation engine that pages the right leader when an event has been open too long. In the afternoon you might pair with the product manager on a self-service onboarding flow, review code, and prototype an AI-drafted event summary for Call Leaders. Your work shows up every time an issue is caught earlier, resolved faster, or never happens at all.

About the team
The LeoNOC and LIM Operations Tooling team builds the operational products that keep a global space and terrestrial telecom network healthy and its operations efficient. We sit next to the people who use our tools, the Network Operations Center and the Incident Management Team. We measure success by how much faster, quieter, and more automated operations become as the network scales toward and beyond general availability.
- 3+ years of non-internship professional software development experience
- 2+ years of non-internship design or architecture (design patterns, reliability and scaling) of new and existing systems experience
- 1+ years of software development engineer or related occupational experience
- 1+ years of designing and developing large-scale, multi-tiered, multi-threaded, embedded or distributed software applications, tools, systems, and services using: C#, C++, Java, or Perl experience
- 1+ years of Object Oriented Design experience
- Bachelor's degree or foreign equivalent in Computer Science, Engineering, Mathematics, or a related field
- Experience programming with at least one software programming language
- 3+ years of full software development life cycle, including coding standards, code reviews, source control management, build processes, testing, and operations experience
- Bachelor's degree in computer science or equivalent
- Experience building complex software systems that have been successfully delivered to customers
- Experience designing or architecting (design patterns, reliability and scaling) of new and existing systems
- Experience in debugging, profiling, and implementing software engineering best practices in large-scale systems
- Bachelor's degree or equivalent
